settings.parameter_basis: USGS1995 CO/H2O/CO2/H2/N2 thermochemistry and restricted water-gas-shift equilibrium; gas feed, geometry, constant viscosity, surface tension, matrix heat capacity and heat conductance are explicit virtual scenario definitions.
settings.scope: Closed spherical pore with ideal gas CO+H2O<=>CO2+H2 equilibrium and inertN2. Initial gas is equilibrated at initial T before timezero; preparation heat is outside the ledger. No finite reaction kinetics, graphite, methane, gas escape, actual brick or fullC/H/O equilibrium qualification.

sources.title: Cavitation and Bubble Dynamics
sources.use: Full Rayleigh-Plesset surface traction and closed ideal-gas pressure; creeping infinite-matrix limit derived separately.
Vented spherical-shell porosity law only; experimental glass viscosity and glass-bead qualification not transferred to brick.

mechanical_source.selected_model: Finite spherical incompressible Newtonian shell, fixed matrix volume, outer normal traction -p_out, no exterior surface energy, constantT and gamma; closed ideal gas or prescribed pressure venting.
literal_source_cautions: Wadsworthp5prose describeszero porosityat infinite time, but its Eq2.12 has an integrable phi^(-2/3) closure time for constant finite positive viscosity. Distinguish prose from the equation actually used.
Wadsworthp8viscosity prose writes mu=A+B/(T-C); no logarithm is printed while p9figure uses viscosity of10^5to10^13Pa*s. No empirical viscosity parameter admitted until original2014source is checked.

additional_visual_review.scope: Confirmed the literal viscosity expression without log and material/method statements; empirical fit remains unadmitted.

thermal_sources.gas_constant_policy: Historical book R retained for separate same-source nominal calculation.

CO.domain_note: Cp coefficient table prints upper2500K; individual ideal-gas table states2200K. Selected1200K is within both; preserve conflict.

readback.new_network_pdf_access: 403; already available official PDF inspected locally, no new retrieval claimed.

thermal_sources.source_choice: Preserve the complete selected USGS nominal source. Do not silently replace CO entropy with another compilation. Published coefficient-fit covariance and relevant real-char properties remain unknown.

nist_co_cross_source_comparison.classification: Independent published compilation value, not an experimental holdout and not substituted into the USGS model.

thermal_sources.scope: Pure reference graphite and ideal gases; not measured sludge char, finite reaction rate, volatile inventory, or actual brick atmosphere.

thermal_sources.gas_constant_policy: Historical book constant retained consistently with existingC/O phases. Not silently replaced by modernSI R.

visual_review.method: Rendered fullPDF pages and visually checked coefficients and298.15-1200K rows; no hash

thermal_sources.reference_policy: h(T)=hf(298.15K)+integralCp. Formationenthalpy atT subtracts elemental sensible enthalpies, so is not single-species storage h(T).
thermal_sources.rounding_policy: Printed coefficient/reference/table half-last-unit arithmetic enclosures only; no physical fit error or experimental covariance inferred.
thermal_sources.phase_scope: Ideal gas standard-state functions. Below physical condensation temperatures the vapor standard state is a formal reference, not stable liquid-water equilibrium. No saturation/adsorption closure or energy alignment with low-temperature material inferred.

equilibrium_parameters.scope: Restricted ideal gas water-gas-shift equilibrium and closed rigid adiabatic endpoint. No rates, graphite, methane, O2 equilibrium, condensed water, actual kiln or material qualification.
